'''Edward S. Yeung''' is a Chinese-American [[chemist]] who studies [[spectroscopy]] and chromatography. Yeung is a Distinguished Professor Emeritus at [[Iowa State University]]. He was elected as a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref name="ISU">{{cite web |title=Edward S Yeung |url=https://www.chem.iastate.edu/people/edward-yeung |website=Department of Chemistry |publisher=Iowa State University |access-date=5 June 2021}}</ref>   He was a founding co-editor of the ''[[Annual Review of Analytical Chemistry]]'' from 2008 to 2014<ref name="Zare">{{cite journal |last1=Yeung |first1=Edward S. |last2=Zare |first2=Richard N. |title=Preface |journal=Annual Review of Analytical Chemistry |date=13 June 2008 |volume=1 |issue=1 |doi=10.1146/annurev.ac.061308.100001 |url=https://www.annualreviews.org/doi/10.1146/annurev.ac.061308.100001 |access-date=8 September 2021|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Co-editors of the Annual Review of Analytical Chemistry - Volume 7, 2014 |url=https://www.annualreviews.org/db/directory?2014,anchem |website=Annual Reviews Directory |access-date=8 September 2021}}</ref> and has served on the editorial committees of a number of other journals.<ref name="ISU"/>

Yeung was the first person to quantitatively analyze the chemical contents of a single human [[red blood cell]] (erythrocyte).<ref name="Cannon">{{cite journal |last1=Cannon Jr |first1=D. M. |last2=Winograd |first2=N. |author3-link=Andrew G. Ewing |last3=Ewing |first3=A. G. |title=Quantitative Chemical Analysis of Single Cells |journal=Annual Review of Biophysics and Biomolecular Structure |date=June 2000 |volume=29 |issue=1 |pages=239–263 |doi=10.1146/annurev.biophys.29.1.239 |pmid=10940249 |access-date=8 September 2021 |url=https://www.annualreviews.org/doi/full/10.1146/annurev.biophys.29.1.239 |language=en |issn=1056-8700|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name="Hogan">{{cite journal |last1=Hogan |first1=Barry L. |last2=Yeung |first2=Edward S. |title=Single-cell analysis at the level of a single human erythrocyte |journal=TrAC Trends in Analytical Chemistry |date=January 1993 |volume=12 |issue=1 |pages=4–9 |doi=10.1016/0165-9936(93)85007-6 |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/0165993693850076 |access-date=8 September 2021|url-access=subscription }}</ref> His research group has developed a method using [[capillary electrophoresis]] (CE) to identify the [[coenzymes]] [[NAD+]] and [[NADH]] within a cell.<ref name="Lin">{{cite journal |last1=Lin |first1=Yuqing |last2=Trouillon |first2=Raphaël |last3=Safina |first3=Gulnara |last4=Ewing |first4=Andrew G. |title=Chemical Analysis of Single Cells |journal=Analytical Chemistry |date=15 June 2011 |volume=83 |issue=12 |pages=4369–4392 |doi=10.1021/ac2009838 |pmid=21500835 |pmc=3115477 }}</ref> Such developments could lead to improved detection of [[AIDS]], [[cancer]] and genetic diseases such as [[Alzheimer's disease]], [[muscular dystrophy]], and [[Down syndrome]]. Yeung has won four R&D 100 Awards and an Editor's Choice award from R&D Magazine for this pioneering work. He is also the 2002 recipient of the [[American Chemical Society]] Award in Chromatography for his research in chemical separations.<ref name="ISU" /><ref name="Wixom">{{cite book |last1=Wixom |first1=Robert L. |last2=Gehrke |first2=Charles W. |title=Chromatography : a science of discovery |date=2010 |publisher=Wiley |location=Hoboken, N.J. |isbn=978-0-470-28345-5 |pages=193–194 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=pKKoOCsytBMC&pg=PA193 |access-date=8 September 2021}}</ref>
